chapter: Shows, scripts and the Mosby-era names
title: Ray Rovin and the short-lived Music Town record company
summary: Rovin, the Philharmonic program concessionaire, joined Spikes and McCoy in a record company but left after his father died.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Mmmm hmmmmm. I was looking at...oh, "Entire production under supervision of Ray Rovin, Reb Spikes, A. McCoy."
Yeah, Ray Rovin was a white boy that...he hung around up there, and he...at the Philharmonic, he had the song con...er, uh, the...
Yeah, he had the program concession at all...
at the Shrine...for the jazz concerts...at the Philharmonic...

Now, when he was with us up there, we started a record company, and his...he went home one night, and his father died in his arms, so the next day he come over and say, "Reb, I can't go no farther," so he left us. He was a nice fellow.
Yeah. I knew him a few years later when I was working for Gene Norman, and he always had charge of all the programs at all the concerts Gene Norman put on. And I see...you had...

I never did see him after that...after...he was with us in the record company and everything else and... He and Austin and I were the three in it, you know, and finally, he went home one night, and his father, I think he died right in his arms, and he come back, and he...he pulled out.
